MN.process: Delinquent real-property taxes proceed through judgment/redemption and, if not redeemed, property forfeits to the State of Minnesota; counties administer disposition of tax-forfeited land.
MN.sale: Minn. Stat. 282.005 requires an initial public auction by the county auditor to the highest bidder, allows online auction, starts at estimated market value, then may reduce to the statutory minimum bid if unsold.
MN.redeem: Redemption occurs before forfeiture under Chapter 281; periods vary by property/classification and should be confirmed at the county/property level.
MN.interest: Minnesota Revenue lists 7% for 2026 delinquent taxes and for tax-forfeited land sold on contract for deed.

MS.type: TAX LIEN / TAX SALE CERTIFICATE -> TAX DEED IF UNREDEEMED
MS.process: County Tax Collectors sell delinquent real-property taxes annually; Chancery Clerks maintain tax-sale/redemption records. Parcels not purchased are struck to the State, and if not redeemed during the two-year period they are certified to the Secretary of State as tax-forfeited lands.
MS.sale: Annual county sale is generally the last Monday in August, with an optional first-Monday-in-April sale. County-specific platform may be GovEase, another vendor, or local process.
MS.redeem: Official MS Secretary of State rules describe a two-year redemption period after tax sale. County operational pages (Jackson, Lamar, Itawamba) also state two years.
MS.interest: Official county operational pages for Jackson/Lamar/Itawamba state 1.5% per month on the base/initial lien amount; overbid does not earn interest.

MO.type: TAX LIEN CERTIFICATE / COLLECTOR DEED (Chapter 140 general route) JUDICIAL LAND TAX FORECLOSURE / SHERIFF SALE (Chapter 141 opt-in route)
MO.process: For counties using Chapter 140, delinquent real property is offered at a county-collector tax certificate sale. Purchaser receives a certificate of purchase and may later qualify for a collector's deed if statutory notice/title-search requirements are met. Counties may elect to operate wholly or partially under the Land Tax Collection Law. Delinquent land-tax liens proceed through judicial foreclosure rather than the standard Chapter 140 certificate sale for affected parcels.
MO.sale: RSMo 140.150 subjects delinquent property to sale on the fourth Monday in August. County implementation may be in-person or via an officially designated platform. Court judgment precedes sheriff sale; RSMo 141.540 governs advertisement/sheriff sale and RSMo 141.570 addresses title after court confirmation.
MO.redeem: First/second offering: generally one-year absolute redemption plus defeasible redemption until deed. Third offering: 90-day redemption. Current post-third-year sales under the 2026 statute may carry no redemption period. Redemption/equity treatment follows the Chapter 141 judicial process and differs from the standard Chapter 140 certificate redemption model.
MO.interest: Certificate rate may not exceed 10% per year; qualifying subsequent taxes are generally reimbursed with 8% annual interest under RSMo 140.340. Not a standard certificate-interest investment; economics depend on bid, court sale, and parcel-specific liens/terms.

MT.type: TAX LIEN ASSIGNMENT TAX DEED / PUBLIC AUCTION FOR APPLICABLE PARCELS
MT.process: County treasurer attaches a tax lien no later than the first working day in August to delinquent properties for which proper notice was given. The county is initially the possessor of the lien. A private buyer may obtain an assignment after giving the required owner notice and paying delinquent taxes, penalties, interest, and costs. After the redemption period, the county or assignee may proceed toward a tax deed. For the owner-occupied-dwelling auction route created by current Chapter 18 law, an assignee applies for a tax deed and the county treasurer holds a public auction within 60 days of the application.
MT.sale: No statewide lien auction. Investor acquisition is by county-treasurer assignment under MCA 15-17-323; counties must maintain a policy for competing assignment requests. Public tax-deed auction when the Chapter 18 auction route applies; otherwise Chapter 18 also provides direct tax-deed issuance paths depending on parcel/possessor facts. County-specific notices control.
MT.redeem: General redemption deadline is the first working day in August, 3 years after attachment. Certain unimproved subdivided residential/commercial lots with delinquent SID/RSID assessments use a 2-year period. Owner may redeem through the applicable redemption deadline before deed/auction consequences attach; parcel-specific notice obligations apply.
MT.interest: Delinquent taxes generally accrue 5/6 of 1% per month (10% annualized) plus a one-time 2% penalty; assignee economics follow the statutory delinquency rate. Not a certificate-rate auction. The deed-auction economics are the opening bid and auction terms rather than a bid-down interest rate.

NE.process: Generally after three years; qualifying vacant and abandoned real estate may use a two-year timeframe, subject to statutory notice requirements. Nebraska DOR publishes county delinquent-real-property lists submitted by county treasurers and links a statewide 02/2026 Excel file plus county treasurer contact/parcel-search information.
NE.sale: Tax lien certificate; tax sale transfers the tax lien rather than immediate title. First Monday in March; county treasurer/designee continues sale until parcels are sold or offered. Property remaining unsold after public auction proceeds to private sale under § 77-1814.
NE.interest: County treasurer announces rules; round-robin format is authorized. Bidder pays taxes, delinquent interest, and costs; $25 registration fee. 14% per annum on delinquent taxes owed to political subdivisions. Owner or other interested party may redeem before the tax-deed application is received by the county treasurer.

Lien enforcement: Municipal real-property tax liens are enforced under AS 29.45.320-.470, including annual judicial foreclosure procedures.
Foreclosure list: Municipality annually petitions superior court and publishes/posts a foreclosure list for prior-year delinquent taxes.
Routing implication: Census-area baseline must continue at borough/city taxing-jurisdiction level rather than treating the census-area government as a tax-sale authority.

AL.process: All non-public-utility property tax is assessed and collected through 67 county tax offices. DOR publishes weekly county transcripts of tax-delinquent property in State inventory and accepts purchase applications. If State held certificate <3 years purchaser receives assignment; if >3 years purchaser receives tax deed; neither by itself guarantees clear title.
AL.sale: Public tax auction is normally held annually, usually the first Monday in May.
AL.redeem: DOR FAQ states property may be redeemed within three years of sale with taxes, fees and penalties at 12% per annum.
lines: Administration: All non-public-utility property tax is assessed and collected through 67 county tax offices.
Annual tax auction: Public tax auction is normally held annually, usually the first Monday in May.
Redemption / return: DOR FAQ states property may be redeemed within three years of sale with taxes, fees and penalties at 12% per annum.
State-held OTC inventory: DOR publishes weekly county transcripts of tax-delinquent property in State inventory and accepts purchase applications.
State-held conveyance: If State held certificate <3 years purchaser receives assignment; if >3 years purchaser receives tax deed; neither by itself guarantees clear title.

AR.sale: County collectors certify tax-delinquent real estate to the Arkansas Commissioner of State Lands, which administers sales. COSL conducts public auctions of tax-delinquent land and offers qualifying unsold parcels through online post-auction sales. COSL provides official parcel search, auction catalog, mapping and online post-auction platform. COSL sales convey tax-delinquent land through the state sale/deed process; title due diligence remains purchaser responsibility.
AR.redeem: COSL parcel-search guidance states sale is final and redemption must occur by the last business day before the sale.
lines: Administration: County collectors certify tax-delinquent real estate to the Arkansas Commissioner of State Lands, which administers sales.
Sale channels: COSL conducts public auctions of tax-delinquent land and offers qualifying unsold parcels through online post-auction sales.
Current parcel source: COSL provides official parcel search, auction catalog, mapping and online post-auction platform.
Redemption cutoff: COSL parcel-search guidance states sale is final and redemption must occur by the last business day before the sale.
Instrument: COSL sales convey tax-delinquent land through the state sale/deed process; title due diligence remains purchaser responsibility.

CA.process: County Tax Collectors handle current/prior-year delinquencies; BOE publishes contacts for all 58 counties.
CA.sale: BOE staff analysis states residential property generally becomes subject to sale after five years of default and nonresidential commercial property after three years, with statutory notice/board steps. Tax-defaulted property is sold through county tax-sale procedures, including public auction authorized by the Revenue and Taxation Code. Current lists, auction platforms, deposits and re-offer rules are county-specific and must be verified from each county Tax Collector.
lines: Administration: County Tax Collectors handle current/prior-year delinquencies; BOE publishes contacts for all 58 counties.

Tax-defaulted sale: BOE staff analysis states residential property generally becomes subject to sale after five years of default and nonresidential commercial property after three years, with statutory notice/board steps.
Sale form: Tax-defaulted property is sold through county tax-sale procedures, including public auction authorized by the Revenue and Taxation Code.
Current-source requirement: Current lists, auction platforms, deposits and re-offer rules are county-specific and must be verified from each county Tax Collector.

CT.process: Property-tax collection is an exclusive function of municipal government; OPM publishes municipal tax collectors.
CT.sale: Municipal collectors may sell real estate at public auction for delinquent taxes under CGS §12-157.
CT.redeem: Under §12-157, deed is held unrecorded during the statutory redemption period; standard period is six months, with certain qualifying abandoned property subject to a shorter period.
CT.interest: Redemption generally requires purchase price plus statutory interest, stated in current §12-157 as 18% per annum.
lines: Administration: Property-tax collection is an exclusive function of municipal government; OPM publishes municipal tax collectors.
Sale authority: Municipal collectors may sell real estate at public auction for delinquent taxes under CGS §12-157.
Redemption: Under §12-157, deed is held unrecorded during the statutory redemption period; standard period is six months, with certain qualifying abandoned property subject to a shorter period.
Purchaser return: Redemption generally requires purchase price plus statutory interest, stated in current §12-157 as 18% per annum.

DE.process: The monition states the tax judgment and warns that the property may be sold if the judgment is not paid within the statutory notice period.
DE.sale: Delinquent county real-estate taxes may be enforced through the statutory monition method and public sale.
DE.interest: Title 9 separately authorizes sale of delinquent land in Kent and Sussex with notice and court approval. For the statutory land-sale procedure, deed is delayed one year and the owner may redeem during that period by paying purchase money, costs and 20% interest.
lines: Sale method: Delinquent county real-estate taxes may be enforced through the statutory monition method and public sale.
Monition notice: The monition states the tax judgment and warns that the property may be sold if the judgment is not paid within the statutory notice period.
Kent/Sussex sale procedure: Title 9 separately authorizes sale of delinquent land in Kent and Sussex with notice and court approval.
Kent/Sussex redemption: For the statutory land-sale procedure, deed is delayed one year and the owner may redeem during that period by paying purchase money, costs and 20% interest.

GA.process: County Tax Commissioners collect county ad valorem taxes; Georgia DOR publishes county tax-office links. Georgia DOR states unpaid property taxes may be levied upon and property may ultimately be sold.
GA.sale: County Tax Commissioner is the best official source for county tax-sale and lien questions.
GA.redeem: Georgia tax-sale law provides an initial 12-month redemption period and permits redemption thereafter until the right is foreclosed by statutory notice. The enacted tax-sale redemption provisions include the statutory premium framework associated with O.C.G.A. 48-4-42.
lines: Administration: County Tax Commissioners collect county ad valorem taxes; Georgia DOR publishes county tax-office links.
Tax enforcement: Georgia DOR states unpaid property taxes may be levied upon and property may ultimately be sold.
Redemption period: Georgia tax-sale law provides an initial 12-month redemption period and permits redemption thereafter until the right is foreclosed by statutory notice.
Redemption premium: The enacted tax-sale redemption provisions include the statutory premium framework associated with O.C.G.A. 48-4-42.
Current sale source: County Tax Commissioner is the best official source for county tax-sale and lien questions.

HI.process: Hawaii Department of Taxation states four counties administer real property taxes: Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui and Kauai. Real-property taxation is exercised exclusively by counties, except Kalawao County.
HI.sale: Maui's official delinquent-account page publishes 3+ year delinquent accounts and tax-sale auction information.
HI.redeem: Tax-foreclosure sale mechanics are county-specific under county code; current sale lists and redemption rules must be verified from each county.
lines: Administration: Hawaii Department of Taxation states four counties administer real property taxes: Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui and Kauai.
Constitutional allocation: Real-property taxation is exercised exclusively by counties, except Kalawao County.
Sale structure: Tax-foreclosure sale mechanics are county-specific under county code; current sale lists and redemption rules must be verified from each county.
Maui current source: Maui's official delinquent-account page publishes 3+ year delinquent accounts and tax-sale auction information.

ID.process: Counties levy and collect Idaho property taxes; the State Tax Commission publishes official assessor/treasurer contacts for all counties. Idaho does not use investor tax-lien certificates for real-property delinquency; counties use the tax-deed process.
ID.sale: County Treasurer is the authoritative source for current tax-deed lists/hearings/auctions.
ID.redeem: County tax-deed process begins for parcels more than three years delinquent; current county pages describe the hearing, redemption and later public sale workflow.
lines: Administration: Counties levy and collect Idaho property taxes; the State Tax Commission publishes official assessor/treasurer contacts for all counties.
Investment type: Idaho does not use investor tax-lien certificates for real-property delinquency; counties use the tax-deed process.
Tax deed timing: County tax-deed process begins for parcels more than three years delinquent; current county pages describe the hearing, redemption and later public sale workflow.
Current source: County Treasurer is the authoritative source for current tax-deed lists/hearings/auctions.

IL.sale: County collector offers every delinquent property in the published list for sale until all have been offered. Current law also provides for certain county acquisitions and subsequent tax-deed auctions. Sale dates, registration and delinquent lists are administered by each county collector/treasurer.
IL.interest: Annual county-collector tax sale of delinquent taxes / tax lien certificate interests under Article 21 of the Property Tax Code. Purchaser is the bidder offering the least penalty percentage; current statutory maximum is 9%.
lines: Investment type: Annual county-collector tax sale of delinquent taxes / tax lien certificate interests under Article 21 of the Property Tax Code.
Sale authority: County collector offers every delinquent property in the published list for sale until all have been offered.
Bidding: Purchaser is the bidder offering the least penalty percentage; current statutory maximum is 9%.
County-acquired property: Current law also provides for certain county acquisitions and subsequent tax-deed auctions.
Current source: Sale dates, registration and delinquent lists are administered by each county collector/treasurer.

IN.sale: County treasurer conducts delinquent real-property tax sale and issues tax sale certificates. County treasurer/auditor administers the sale; electronic auctions are used by many counties.
IN.redeem: Tax-sale redemption is governed by IC 6-1.1-25; official 2026 county notices describe the applicable redemption periods.
lines: Sale: County treasurer conducts delinquent real-property tax sale and issues tax sale certificates.
Redemption: Tax-sale redemption is governed by IC 6-1.1-25; official 2026 county notices describe the applicable redemption periods.
Current administration: County treasurer/auditor administers the sale; electronic auctions are used by many counties.

NC.process: County Tax Collectors are appointed by county commissioners; NCDOR publishes official collector web pages.
NC.sale: Tax lien may be foreclosed through judicial sale in the nature of mortgage foreclosure. County collector and county attorney are the operative sources for current foreclosure lists/sales.
lines: Administration: County Tax Collectors are appointed by county commissioners; NCDOR publishes official collector web pages.
Judicial foreclosure: Tax lien may be foreclosed through judicial sale in the nature of mortgage foreclosure.
Current source: County collector and county attorney are the operative sources for current foreclosure lists/sales.

ND.process: Counties determine and collect real-property taxes.
ND.sale: Chapter 57-28 provides foreclosure, tax deed to county, appraisal, annual auction and private sale between annual sales. Chapter 57-28 provides appraisal, annual public sale and private sale between annual sales.
lines: Administration: Counties determine and collect real-property taxes.
Tax deed/disposition: Chapter 57-28 provides foreclosure, tax deed to county, appraisal, annual auction and private sale between annual sales.
Disposition: Chapter 57-28 provides appraisal, annual public sale and private sale between annual sales.

NY.process: ORPTS publishes county property-tax director contacts.
NY.redeem: RPTL §1110 generally provides a two-year redemption period from the lien date, subject to statutory/local variations. Article 11 authorizes in-rem tax foreclosure after statutory redemption timing.
lines: Redemption: RPTL §1110 generally provides a two-year redemption period from the lien date, subject to statutory/local variations.
Foreclosure: Article 11 authorizes in-rem tax foreclosure after statutory redemption timing.
Local contacts: ORPTS publishes county property-tax director contacts.

OH.sale: Unsold certificates can move to negotiated sale or foreclosure routes.
OH.redeem: Owner may redeem under ORC 5721.38 before specified foreclosure milestones by paying certificate redemption price and applicable amounts.
OH.interest: County treasurer may auction tax certificates; bidding starts at 18% simple interest and is bid down to zero.
lines: Tax certificate auction: County treasurer may auction tax certificates; bidding starts at 18% simple interest and is bid down to zero.
Redemption: Owner may redeem under ORC 5721.38 before specified foreclosure milestones by paying certificate redemption price and applicable amounts.
Hybrid routes: Unsold certificates can move to negotiated sale or foreclosure routes.

OK.sale: County treasurer administers delinquent real-property sale notices. Property remaining delinquent/unredeemed proceeds through county resale; resale notice must include parcel/owner/time/place and online-auction website if applicable. Oklahoma tax-sale process can issue a County Treasurer certificate; statutory deed/resale rights follow if unredeemed.
lines: Administration: County treasurer administers delinquent real-property sale notices.
Resale: Property remaining delinquent/unredeemed proceeds through county resale; resale notice must include parcel/owner/time/place and online-auction website if applicable.
Tax-sale certificate/deed: Oklahoma tax-sale process can issue a County Treasurer certificate; statutory deed/resale rights follow if unredeemed.

OR.process: County property-tax offices administer local property taxes. ORS Chapter 312 governs judicial foreclosure of delinquent property-tax liens and transfer to county. County disposition of tax-foreclosed property is governed by ORS Chapter 275.
lines: Administration: County property-tax offices administer local property taxes.
Foreclosure: ORS Chapter 312 governs judicial foreclosure of delinquent property-tax liens and transfer to county.
Disposition: County disposition of tax-foreclosed property is governed by ORS Chapter 275.

PA.process: Act 542 creates county Tax Claim Bureaus subject to statutory exceptions.
PA.sale: Section 601 schedules annual upset sale between the second Monday of September and October 1, subject to continuances. Article VI provides judicial sale and repository sale pathways.
lines: Tax Claim Bureau: Act 542 creates county Tax Claim Bureaus subject to statutory exceptions.
Upset sale: Section 601 schedules annual upset sale between the second Monday of September and October 1, subject to continuances.
Unsold property: Article VI provides judicial sale and repository sale pathways.

RI.sale: Municipal tax collectors administer local tax collection and sales.
RI.redeem: Chapter 44-9 governs tax sales, tax titles, redemption and foreclosure. Chapter 44-9 includes redemption from purchaser and foreclosure of redemption procedures.
lines: Local authority: Municipal tax collectors administer local tax collection and sales.
Tax sale law: Chapter 44-9 governs tax sales, tax titles, redemption and foreclosure.
Redemption: Chapter 44-9 includes redemption from purchaser and foreclosure of redemption procedures.

SC.process: Forfeited Land Commissions receive qualifying unsold property and later dispose of it.
SC.sale: County delinquent-tax sale process is governed by Title 12 Chapter 51.
SC.redeem: Real property has a statutory 12-month redemption period after delinquent tax sale.
lines: Sale authority: County delinquent-tax sale process is governed by Title 12 Chapter 51.
Redemption: Real property has a statutory 12-month redemption period after delinquent tax sale.
FLC: Forfeited Land Commissions receive qualifying unsold property and later dispose of it.

SD.sale: Tax deed eligibility generally begins no sooner than three years after sale, subject to statutory limits and notice.
SD.redeem: Property may be redeemed before tax deed issuance.
SD.interest: Annual delinquent real-property tax sale is on the third Monday in December; lowest interest-rate bid prevails if competitive.
lines: Annual tax sale: Annual delinquent real-property tax sale is on the third Monday in December; lowest interest-rate bid prevails if competitive.
Redemption: Property may be redeemed before tax deed issuance.
Tax deed timing: Tax deed eligibility generally begins no sooner than three years after sale, subject to statutory limits and notice.

TN.sale: Tennessee law provides court-supervised sale of property for delinquent taxes. Counties must maintain/publish listings of parcels acquired through delinquent tax sales under §67-5-2511.
TN.redeem: For orders confirming sale on/after July 1, 2026: delinquency of three years or less has a one-year redemption period; more than three years has a 90-day period.
lines: Tax sale: Tennessee law provides court-supervised sale of property for delinquent taxes.
County-owned parcels: Counties must maintain/publish listings of parcels acquired through delinquent tax sales under §67-5-2511.
Redemption effective 7/1/2026: For orders confirming sale on/after July 1, 2026: delinquency of three years or less has a one-year redemption period; more than three years has a 90-day period.

TX.process: Comptroller county directory publishes Tax Assessor-Collector and appraisal district contacts.
TX.sale: Texas Tax Code Chapter 34 governs tax sales following delinquent-tax foreclosure or seizure.
TX.interest: Residence homestead, agricultural land and mineral interests generally have a two-year redemption period with 25% first-year and 50% second-year premium; other property generally has a 180-day redemption period with 25% premium.
lines: Tax sale: Texas Tax Code Chapter 34 governs tax sales following delinquent-tax foreclosure or seizure.

Redemption: Residence homestead, agricultural land and mineral interests generally have a two-year redemption period with 25% first-year and 50% second-year premium; other property generally has a 180-day redemption period with 25% premium.
County contacts: Comptroller county directory publishes Tax Assessor-Collector and appraisal district contacts.

UT.sale: County auditor conducts the tax sale in May or June and may use an electronic process.
UT.redeem: Property not redeemed after four years enters the tax-sale listing; redemption remains available before the sale.
lines: Redemption / listing: Property not redeemed after four years enters the tax-sale listing; redemption remains available before the sale.
Sale timing: County auditor conducts the tax sale in May or June and may use an electronic process.

VA.process: County and city treasurers collect local/state taxes and delinquent taxes.
VA.sale: Virginia law authorizes proceedings to sell real estate for delinquent taxes under Chapter 39. Qualifying lower-value parcels may be sold at public auction under §58.1-3975 after statutory delinquency and notice conditions.
lines: Local collection: County and city treasurers collect local/state taxes and delinquent taxes.
Judicial sale: Virginia law authorizes proceedings to sell real estate for delinquent taxes under Chapter 39.
Nonjudicial small-property sale: Qualifying lower-value parcels may be sold at public auction under §58.1-3975 after statutory delinquency and notice conditions.

VT.type: MUNICIPAL TAX SALE / REDEEMABLE TAX DEED
VT.process: Municipal tax collectors enforce delinquent real-property taxes; a tax sale may proceed under 32 V.S.A. chapter 133 after statutory delinquency thresholds and notice.
VT.sale: Public auction by the municipal tax collector.
VT.redeem: Owner generally has one year to redeem after sale under 32 V.S.A. §5260.
VT.interest: 1% per month during the statutory redemption period.

WA.process: County treasurer initiates tax foreclosure after statutory delinquency and obtains judgment before sale.
WA.sale: Public tax-foreclosure auction; county platform varies.
WA.redeem: Redemption generally remains available through close of business on the day before sale, subject to limited statutory post-sale exceptions.
WA.interest: Varies by statutory charges; underwrite from county judgment/minimum bid rather than assuming an investor certificate yield.

WI.process: Wisconsin counties/municipalities may foreclose delinquent taxes using tax deed, certificate foreclosure, or in-rem foreclosure methods under Chapter 75.
WI.sale: Sale/disposition occurs after the applicable foreclosure method; county practices vary.
WI.redeem: Redemption and foreclosure timing depend on Chapter 75 method and county process; verify locally.
WI.interest: Not treated as a standardized investor tax-lien yield product.

WV.process: Delinquent properties may move through sheriff tax-sale procedures and, when not sold/redeemed, into State Auditor certified-to-state/no-bid processes.
WV.sale: County sheriff sale plus State Auditor county-collections/bidding platform for applicable certified-to-state property.
WV.redeem: Redemption rights and purchaser-stage requirements are governed by W. Va. Code Chapter 11A, Article 3.
WV.interest: Statutory purchaser/redemption charges vary by stage; Chapter 11A includes 1% per month in specified redemption calculations.

WY.process: County treasurer conducts annual delinquent-tax sale of tax liens; purchaser receives certificate rather than immediate property title.
WY.sale: County tax-lien sale; procedures/registration vary by county.
WY.redeem: Certificate redemption is governed by Wyoming Title 39; deed process follows statutory notice and waiting requirements.
WY.interest: For modern tax-sale certificates, statutory return includes 15% per annum plus a 3% penalty on the purchase amount, subject to the statute and county application.

KS.process: Kansas counties judicially foreclose delinquent real-estate taxes and sell property after statutory foreclosure proceedings.
KS.sale: County judicial foreclosure sale / public auction rather than an investor certificate sale.
KS.redeem: Redemption rights are handled before and through the judicial foreclosure process; verify case-specific status.
KS.interest: Not a standardized investor certificate yield product.

KY.process: County clerks sell certificates of delinquency to registered third-party purchasers under Kentucky law and DOR regulations.
KY.sale: Annual county-clerk sale; each county publishes certificates and registration details.
KY.redeem: Property owners retain statutory payment/redemption rights until lien enforcement/foreclosure is completed.
KY.interest: Interest/fees are statutory and certificate-specific; use DOR rules and current certificate data.

LA.process: Effective January 1, 2026 Louisiana shifted to a tax-lien-certificate framework, with parish tax collectors and political subdivisions administering liens.
LA.sale: Tax-lien certificate sale/assignment under the 2026 statutory regime; local implementation and platform vary.
LA.redeem: Redemption remains statutory and lien-specific; verify current certificate and parish rules.
LA.interest: Competitive interest terms are governed by the new statute and local sale terms.

ME.process: Municipal tax collectors record tax-lien mortgages; if not redeemed the lien can automatically foreclose, creating tax-acquired property.
ME.sale: After foreclosure, sale of tax-acquired property follows statutory broker/market-sale procedures; Maine Revenue Services handles Unorganized Territory.
ME.redeem: Title 36 §943 provides an 18-month redemption period from filing of the tax-lien certificate, subject to notice rules.
ME.interest: Interest/costs accrue under Maine property-tax law; verify municipal account amounts.

MD.process: Local jurisdictions sell tax liens/certificates for delinquent real-property taxes under Maryland Tax-Property Article.
MD.sale: Annual jurisdiction tax sale; method/platform varies by county/city.
MD.redeem: Owner may redeem until the right of redemption is finally foreclosed under the statute.
MD.interest: Interest rate and purchaser charges vary by jurisdiction/statute; use current local sale terms.

MA.process: Cities and towns enforce unpaid real-estate taxes through tax taking or tax sale, creating a tax title that can later be assigned or foreclosed.
MA.sale: Municipal tax taking, tax-title assignment, or tax sale; foreclosure proceeds through Land Court or applicable low-value process.
MA.redeem: Right of redemption continues until final foreclosure; current law generally requires a waiting period before foreclosure petition.
MA.interest: Mass.gov states tax-title accounts earn 8% simple interest annually under the post-2024 rules.

MI.process: Michigan uses a three-year delinquency, forfeiture, and foreclosure process; the Foreclosing Governmental Unit disposes of foreclosed property.
MI.sale: Public foreclosure auctions; state-FGU counties use the officially designated Tax-Sale.info provider.
MI.redeem: Redemption rights expire at the statutory foreclosure deadline before auction/disposition.
MI.interest: This is a deed/foreclosure acquisition process rather than a standardized investor tax-lien yield certificate.

AZ.process: County treasurer sells tax liens/certificates for delinquent real property taxes under Arizona Title 42.
AZ.sale: Annual county tax-lien sale; interest is bid down from the statutory maximum.
AZ.redeem: Redemption is generally available during the statutory certificate period before foreclosure.
AZ.interest: Statutory maximum bid rate is 16% before bid-down; verify county sale terms.

CO.process: County treasurers sell delinquent real-property tax liens; later treasurer-deed procedures are governed by current Title 39 and 2026 amendments.
CO.sale: County tax-lien sale; auction platform and bidding vary by county.
CO.redeem: Redemption remains available until the statutory deed process is completed.
CO.interest: 13% statutory redemption interest effective 2026-10-01; county sale premiums/fees remain separate.

FL.process: Delinquent real-property taxes are sold as tax certificates; eligible certificates can later support an application for tax deed.
FL.sale: Annual tax-certificate sale using bid-down interest; tax-deed sale follows statutory application.
FL.redeem: Tax deed application generally cannot begin until the certificate has been outstanding for the statutory period.
FL.interest: Certificate rate is bid down from 18%, subject to Florida statutory minimum-interest rules.

IA.process: County treasurers conduct annual delinquent-tax sales and issue tax-sale certificates under Iowa Code chapter 446.
IA.sale: Annual county tax sale, commonly via IowaTaxAuction where designated; unsold items may move to adjourned/public-bidder processes.
IA.redeem: Redemption and notice rights are governed by Iowa Code chapter 447 after the certificate sale.
IA.interest: Iowa certificates accrue statutory interest under Chapters 446-447; underwrite from current county terms.
